messages:
maya: Heads up, OpenSSL just published 3.2.1 advisory with a limited PoC in the wild. Vendor has a backport we can apply. Need to decide patch priority + schedule: SLA exposure, public exposure window, and how we handle Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
jonathan: Do we know exploitability? any confirmed active exploitation at scale? :eyes:
maya: Vendor notes 'limited reports of PoC' and a moderate-high risk for TLS termination on edge. Affects our hosted TLS proxies and Dedicated instances that terminate customer traffic. Private deployments only get patches if customers apply them.
li: For Hosted we should do a staged canary. Need rollback and connection-drain plan. Suggest waves: 3% -> 15% -> 50% -> 100%, 30m between waves with health checks. Also add TLS handshake metrics and 5xx rate monitoring.
ana: (typo) ana: From a product/customer standpoint: Dedicated customers expect scheduled maintenance. We should not auto-force patch Dedicated without sales/support buy-in. Hosted = force; Dedicated = opt-in scheduled backport next week; Private = advisory + patch bundle.
jonathan: Agreed. Hosted rollout ASAP. SLA risk if we cause a broad restart; aim for zero-downtime via connection draining + graceful restarts. If we see >0.5% increase in TLS failures for 15m we abort.
maya: Proposed schedule: Hosted canary today 18:00 UTC (3%), if green expand to 25% at 18:45, 75% at 20:00, finish by 00:00 UTC. Dedicated backports scheduled next Tue/Wed windows; Private gets patch and instructions. Who owns customer comms?
ana: ana: I'll draft the comms and notify support/sales. Flagging a couple enterprise clients in APAC with blackout windows — cc @sales for coordination.
patchbot: Patch job queued: openssl-3.2.1-backport on ci-nightly #1782. Canary deploy helper:

```
./deploy_canary --service=edge-proxy --percent=3 --image=redwood/openssl:3.2.1-backport
```

li: Monitoring hooks to add before canary:
- TLS handshake error rate (per-host)
- Edge 5xx rate
- Latency p50/p95
If any metric breaches thresholds for 15m -> automated rollback/abort. Suggested threshold: TLS errors >0.5% or 5xx increase >1%.
jonathan: Rollback command and automation ready:

```
./rollback --service=edge-proxy --to-tag=stable && ./drain-lb --service=edge-proxy
```
Will add to runbook and create a short automation to kick rollback on abort.
maya: OK locking this in. I'll update the incident tracker + runbook and post the finalized plan in #incidents. ana will send customer comms. li/jonathan to own rollout automation and rollback testing. patchbot will kick the build. Thanks — will follow up after the first canary wave. :white_check_mark:
